name: Milwaukee
legalEntityNote: Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation is a TTI subsidiary. TTI parent reporting, regional Milwaukee entities, factories, distributors and service partners can represent different levels of responsibility.
headline: Milwaukee ownership, cordless cleaning equipment and professional platform strategy
description: A source-backed profile of Milwaukee's TTI ownership, M12 and M18 cleaning equipment, professional-channel strategy and model-level supply-chain checks.
metaDescription: Milwaukee profile: TTI ownership, M12 and M18 vacuums, dust management, manufacturing, channels and buyer checks.
disclaimer: World Clean Biz is an independent industry publication and is not affiliated with Milwaukee Tool or Techtronic Industries. Parent-company disclosures do not identify the factory or seller for every Milwaukee SKU.

ownership.summary: Techtronic Industries Company Limited owns Milwaukee. TTI acquired the Milwaukee brand and power-tool business in 2005, and its 2025 annual report lists Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation as an indirectly held 100%-owned principal subsidiary.

leadership.name: A. H. Petersen
leadership.context: Milwaukee's official company story traces the business to A. H. Petersen's 1924 founding of the Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation.

productPortfolio.name: M12 wet-dry and portable vacuums
productPortfolio.positioning: Compact professional cleaners use the 12-volt platform for service, installation and confined-space cleanup.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Confirm bare-tool versus kit configuration, battery requirement, filtration and regional electrical standards.

productPortfolio.name: M18 wet-dry vacuums and dust extractors
productPortfolio.positioning: Higher-capacity cleaners and dust-management systems serve jobsite and trade-specific applications.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Match dust class, filter, hose, tool activation, runtime and compliance to the application.

productPortfolio.name: Dust-management accessories
productPortfolio.positioning: Extractors, shrouds, adapters and drilling solutions connect cleaning to Milwaukee's professional tool ecosystem.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: System compatibility depends on the exact tool, extractor, hose diameter and regional certification.

productPortfolio.name: M12, M18, MX FUEL and PACKOUT systems
productPortfolio.positioning: The wider cordless and storage platforms support Milwaukee's end-to-end professional jobsite strategy.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Shared branding does not make every pack, charger, attachment or market SKU interchangeable.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: TTI's annual report lists Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation as a wholly owned principal subsidiary engaged in trading and manufacturing power equipment products.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Use the product declaration and label to determine the responsible Milwaukee entity for the exact model.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: TTI operates manufacturing, engineering and sourcing locations across North America, Asia and Europe.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Do not infer product origin from Milwaukee's Wisconsin headquarters.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: Milwaukee's product pages and manuals identify model-specific configurations, compliance and service information.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Match the model suffix, voltage, destination market and production date before ordering.

marketsChannels.evidence: Milwaukee positions itself for professional trades and sells through authorized tool distributors and retail partners.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Use an authorized partner to preserve authenticity, warranty and service eligibility.

marketsChannels.evidence: The official site separates product information, authorized buying routes, service centers and warranty registration.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Confirm the destination market's authorized distributor and service network.

marketsChannels.evidence: TTI describes Milwaukee as a global professional platform with R&D headquartered in Brookfield, Wisconsin.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Verify the contracting entity, importer and warranty provider for each country.

competitivePosition.summary: World Clean Biz assessment: Milwaukee's cleaning advantage comes from professional user access, dense M12 and M18 ecosystems and integration with jobsite dust-management workflows. Its risk for buyers is configuration complexity: tool-only packs, battery systems, compliance variants and distributor authorization all require model-level control.
